findings.current: Even now that I had reached the Supreme Peak realm, he was a close yet infinitely distant existence to me, someone whose modern common sense remained rooted deep within him.
findings.defect: The draft attaches modern common sense to the Chairman, but the source says it is rooted in Taekyung. This reverses the subject of a characterization detail.
findings.rationale: The modifier 현대의 상식이 뿌리박힌 내게 describes the narrator, not the Chairman.
findings.replacement: Even now that I had reached the Supreme Peak realm, to me—with modern common sense still rooted deep in my bones—he felt both close and infinitely distant.
findings.source: 초절정의 경지에 오른 지금에도 현대의 상식이 뿌리박힌 내게 그는 가까우면서도 한없이 먼 존재다.

findings.current: The continent existing under the rule of a vast empire was the center of that world.
findings.defect: The draft changes 대국, a great or powerful nation, into an empire, adding an imperial political structure not stated in the source.
findings.rationale: 대국 denotes a large or powerful country; it does not establish that the state is an empire.
findings.replacement: The center of that world was a continent ruled by a vast and powerful nation.
findings.source: 거대한 대국의 통치 아래 존재하는 대륙이 저쪽 세상의 중심이다.

findings.current: What kind of reassuring bullshit was that? It sounded like he was happily stuffing himself with a bowl of gukbap.
findings.defect: The second sentence invents Wei Penghu happily eating and overexplains the wordplay. The source makes a compact pun on 든든하다, which can mean both reassuring and satisfyingly filling.
findings.rationale: This retains the reassuring/hearty pun without adding a physical action or explaining the punchline after delivering it.
findings.replacement: What was this nonsense about feeling reassured? Was he talking about a hearty bowl of gukbap or something?
findings.source: 이게 무슨 든든하게 국밥 말아먹는 소리냐.

findings.current: “Nice to meet you, Teacher Jin. This old man is Shao Yang, the state chairman of the People’s Republic of China.”
findings.defect: Shao Yang contradicts the binding established romanization Xiao Yang.
findings.rationale: The terminology ledger explicitly establishes 샤오 양 as Xiao Yang.
findings.replacement: “Nice to meet you, Teacher Jin. This old man is Xiao Yang, the state chairman of the People’s Republic of China.”
findings.source: 「반갑소, 진 선생. 이 늙은이는 중화인민공화국의 국가 주석을 맡고 있는 샤오 양이라 하오.」

findings.defect: The name is re-romanized contrary to the binding Xiao Yang ledger entry.
findings.rationale: The terminology ledger explicitly establishes 샤오 양 as Xiao Yang.

findings.current: But at least the old man continuing to speak before all of us—including me—carried a kind of qi entirely different from either of those things.
findings.defect: The draft omits Xiao Yang’s name and office, weakening the source’s deliberate identification of the old man as China’s Chairman.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly apposes 샤오 양 중국 주석 to the old man and should not drop either his established name or his office.
findings.replacement: But at least from the old man continuing to speak before all of us—including me—Chairman Xiao Yang of China, I sensed a kind of qi entirely different from either of those things.
findings.source: 하지만 적어도 지금 나를 포함한 모두의 앞에서 말을 이어 가는 노인, 샤오 양 중국 주석에게는 그런 것과는 전혀 다른 종류의 기(氣)가 느껴졌다.

summary: One critical subject reversal, one worldbuilding terminology error, one added-action joke expansion, and three violations of the binding Xiao Yang romanization.
